description: H377 PROPOSED: Network Momentum via lead-lag spillover across asset classes. Source arXiv:2501.07135 (Li, Ferreira 2025). Systematic trend-following that combines univariate trend indicators with cross-sectional network momentum to capture lead-lag spillover between markets. Applied to H026/H041a ETF rotation universe: when one ETF (e.g., XLE energy) is trending, its sector peers and downstream supply-chain ETFs may exhibit lagged momentum — detect with learned lead-lag graph, tilt toward lagged beneficiaries. Sharpe 1.74 over 20 years on 64 commodity futures; adapting to ETF universe.

patch.content: h377_status: PROPOSED (2026-07-06) — Network Momentum via Cross-ETF Lead-Lag Spillover. Source: Li & Ferreira (2025) "Follow the Leader: Enhancing Systematic Trend-Following Using Network Momentum" arXiv:2501.07135. Key finding: combining univariate trend indicators with cross-sectional network momentum that captures lead-lag spillover relationships (when asset A trends, asset B tends to follow N days later) delivers statistically significant improvements in Sharpe ratio, return skewness, and downside performance vs pure univariate trend following. Backtested on 64 commodity futures over 20 years, Sharpe 1.74. H377 adapts to H026+H041a ETF universe (25+19 assets): (1) compute pairwise lead-lag relationships among ETFs using rolling cross-correlation matrix (2-week lags, 6-month window); (2) when the top-ranked ETF by 12m momentum also has strong lead-lag influence over other universe members (i.e., is a 'leader'), increase position size by 25%; (3) if a 'follower' ETF (identified as lagging a current leader by 2-4 weeks) enters the top-2 ranked ETFs, include it alongside the leader rather than applying standard top-1 selection. Universe: H026 25-ETF + H041a 19-ETF combined (40 unique ETFs). Signal: 12m momentum (H026 canonical) + network lead-lag tilt. IS: 2008-2017, OOS: 2018-2026. Gate: OOS Sharpe > 1.300 (meaningful improvement over H026 canonical OOS ~1.2 pre-OB). Key caveat: ETF lead-lag may be sparser than commodity futures (ETFs are more diversified); energy-sector supply chain links (XLE → XLB, XLI) and bond-equity rotation (TLT → SPY with ~1-month lag in regime shifts) are the most promising candidate pairs. Script: backtesting/daily/run_h377.py (to be written).
